Paranormal tours at Preston Castle explore ghostly encounters and preserve history

IONE, Calif. —

Preston Castle in Ione, California, a former reform school for boys known for its harsh conditions, is now a hub for paranormal tours aimed at exploring its eerie history and preserving the site.

Francisco Benavides, Preston Castle's paranormal team leader, and Justin Dieteman, a paranormal investigator, lead these tours at various times throughout the year. They joined the host of California Tonight, Edie Lambert, to discuss the tours and the encounters they've experienced in the castle.

"We have hundreds of guests year-round," Benavides said. "From experienced investigators to people that are doing it for the first time, we get them familiar with the devices, talk about some of the history, give them a tour of the castle, and then we get out there and start investigating different methods."

Dieteman explained the tools used during investigations, including an EMF reader and a spirit box, which sweeps through radio stations rapidly to detect potential spirit communication. "In theory, it's a way to get communication from the spirits because the sweeping radio stations go so fast that it will not let the full words come through," Dieteman said.

During one tour, Dieteman captured a photo in the castle's infirmary that appeared to show the shadowy figure of a boy near a window. "I was seeing, like the heat coming off a hood of a car, so I just started snapping pictures," Dieteman said. "I didn't know this until about two days later when I was going through pictures and zoomed in on it. If you look carefully in the corner, there's a boy standing kind of near the window, and you can see he's wearing a blue shirt."

Benavides recalled another eerie moment from the same night. "I'm walking down one of the long hallways, as I'm walking back towards Justin, and I hear footsteps behind me. I start rushing towards him, he snaps a picture, and in the picture, there's sure enough a full shadow figure. You can see the legs and everything," he said.

In addition to ghost tours, Preston Castle hosts events like "The Haunt," where volunteers dress up to create a fun and spooky experience. "We had over 70 kids here with us this year, and they did a phenomenal job." Benavides emphasized that these efforts aim to preserve the castle's history, as parts of the building are in disrepair. They're currently raising money to fix the roof, the east wing, and the porch on the east side of the castle. The entire third floor remains off-limits due to its deteriorated condition, highlighting the importance of restoration efforts. All proceeds from events go toward preserving the historic site.

"It's very important," said Benavides. "We're very passionate."
